additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
Now I have two strong candidates for NVPF||HC full cells with low-temperature electrolytes:

Candidate A (baseline from 0036 Lin 2019): 1 M NaClO4 in EC/PC (1:1 v/v) — measured in Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3||HC coin cell at 25, 0, -20 °C. At -20 °C: significant drop, unstable SEI, fast fading. Capacity at 0 °C = 244 mAh/g (based on anode mass). The safe reversible no-plating limit = 250 mAh/g at -20 °C (from HC half-cell with same electrolyte).

Candidate B (0023 Hu 2024): 0.8 M NaPF6 + 0.2 M NaBF4 in DEGDME (BPG) — NVPF||HC full cell; full cell tested at -10, 25, 60 °C (not -20). Full cell at -10 °C: 58 mAh/g after 700 cycles at 1C. Cathode half-cell at -25 °C shows 99 mAh/g. Hmm, the full cell was not tested at -20.

Candidate C (0070 Xia 2025): 1 M NaDFOB in G2 (diglyme) — HC//NFPP pouch cell, -40 to 60 °C. But cathode is NFPP, not NVPF. However NVPF electrode also tested (from the chunk: "Both the Na3V2(PO4)3 and Na3V2(PO4)2F3 electrodes show high cycling stability over 200 cycles (Figures S8 and S9)"). That's NVPF with NaDFOB-G2, but not in full cell with HC at -20.

Hmm. What's the best electrolyte selection for NVPF||HC at -20 °C?

The task: "determine a reversible no-plating capacity limit for a Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3||hard-carbon sodium-ion full cell at -20 C while selecting an appropriate electrolyte."

Honestly, the key deterministic result is from paper 0036: 250 mAh g⁻¹ (based on HC anode mass) is the safe, reversible, no-plating capacity limit at -20 °C, established with in situ XRD/Raman; plating starts ~300 mAh/g; at 300 mAh/g CE drops to 95.3%. And the full cell with that same 1 M NaClO4/EC:PC electrolyte fades rapidly at -20 °C → electrolyte must be improved.

So the design output: recommend an electrolyte for NVPF||HC at -20 °C, and state the capacity limit as 250 mAh/g (anode basis) i.e. ~306 mAh/g at 25 °C full cell basis... Actually the capacity of the full cell at 25 °C is 306 mAh/g based on anode mass. The N/P ratio is 2.5 by weight.

Hmm — the full cell's reversible capacity at -20 °C would be limited by the no-plating limit: 250 mAh/g on anode basis. But at -20 °C the full cell delivers less than that due to resistance. Actually 0036 reports full cell at 0 °C "stable capacity retention of 244 mAh g⁻¹". At -20 °C, "significant drop in capacity... particularly during first 5 cycles."

So the no-plating capacity limit at -20 °C = 250 mAh g⁻¹ based on HC anode mass, which corresponds to ~82% of the room-temperature capacity. Hmm, we need to be careful: is 250 mAh/g a "full-cell operating capacity limit" or a "half-cell HC charging limit"? It's the HC half-cell capacity limit without plating. In the full cell, the capacity on anode basis at -20 °C would need to be capped at 250 mAh/g to avoid plating.

Now, electrolyte candidates. Let me consider what's most defensible:
- Candidate 1: 1 M NaClO4 in EC/PC (1:1 v/v) — the reference baseline used in the target full cell with measured -20 °C behavior (fading). 
- Candidate 2: 0.8 M NaPF6 + 0.2 M NaBF4 in DEGDME (BPG) — NVPF||HC full cell demonstrated at -10/25/60 °C; cathode half-cell at -25 °C.
- Candidate 3: 1 M NaDFOB in G2 — HC//NFPP pouch cell -40 to 60 °C.

I should probably also look for the 0033 paper (Li 2026, solvent co-intercalation electrolyte, Ah-level pouch cells at low temperatures, HC). Let me check its composition — it may include NVPF full cell. Actually the abstract says "Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level pouch cells at low temperatures". Let me check if it has NVPF cathode.

Also 0029 Li 2024 (NaPF6 in G1 diglyme-ish ether) — HC electrodes at -20 °C.

Given cost/effort constraints, I think the strongest set is:
1. Baseline carbonate (1 M NaClO4 EC:PC 1:1 v/v) — measured in the exact target full cell at -20 °C.
2. Dual-salt ether BPG (0.8 M NaPF6 + 0.2 M NaBF4 in DEGDME) — measured in the exact target full cell (NVPF||HC), but at -10 °C not -20 °C.
3. NaDFOB-G2 (1 M) — HC full cell but with NFPP cathode; NVPF electrode tested at RT only.

Hmm, for the electrolyte selection at -20 °C we need candidates with -20 °C evidence in NVPF||HC. None exactly. Let me do one more search for NVPF||HC full cell at -20 with ether electrolyte.

Let me search: "NVPF hard carbon full cell -20 °C ether electrolyte", and also check 0033 paper's cathode.

Also, I should use query_formulation_space as required. Let me gather evidence chunks first.

Let me do a couple more targeted searches.

All button cells (CR2032-type) were assembled in an argon-filled glovebox (MIKROUNA of Universal, $O_{2} < 0.01$ ppm, $H_{2}O < 0.01$ ppm). As for the fabrication of the positive electrode, a uniform slurry (active material, carbon black, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 6:3:1 mixed in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidinone) was coated on the aluminum foil and dried in vacuum at 70 °C for 12 h. The mass of active material loading was controlled at 1–2 mg. Metallic sodium plate was used as anode, and glass fiber (Whatman, GF/F) was used as separator. The solution consisted of 1 M NaClO $_{4}$ dissolved in ethylene carbonate

![](images/799395ba1007a706b8bc62ff2dd3bd48ca8c52a9cadeedce6775aa4cd11f504c.jpg)

(EC) and propylene carbonate (PC) (1:1 in $\nu/\mathrm{v}$ ) with 5 vol% fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) was employed as an electrolyte. The battery test system (NEWARE CT-4008) was used for galvanostatic charge/discharge measurement with various current densities at a voltage range of 2.5–4.5 V versus $\mathrm{Na}^{+}/\mathrm{Na}$ . Cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements were performed on the CHI760e electrochemical workstation (CH, Shanghai, China) over the potential range of 2.5–4.5 V and disparate sweep rates. The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements were implemented by CHI760e with the frequency ranging from $10^{-2}$ to $10^{5}$ Hz with an alternating current amplitude of 5 mV. For the preparation of hard carbon (HC) anode, the slurry consisted of HC, carbon black, and PVDF in a weight ratio of 8:1:1 mixed in NMP, was coated on the copper foil and dried in vacuum for 12 h. The mass of active material loading on the anode of NVPF/CNTs half cells was controlled at 0.5–1 mg. The NVPF/CNTs||HC full cells were assembled based on CR2032-type coin battery, and tested at the voltage range of 1.5–4.4 V.

additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
Paper 0391 (Lei 2024): 
- Electrolyte: 1 M NaClO4 in EC/PC (1:1 v/v) with 5 vol% FEC.
- NVPF/CNTs||HC full cells (CR2032), pre-sodiated HC, 1.5–4.4 V.
- At -20 °C: NVPF/CNTs half-cell (vs Na) 96.8 mAh/g at 0.1 A/g, 95.7% retention after 900 cycles / abstract says 98% after 500 cycles at -20 °C. That's a cathode half-cell measurement against Na metal, NOT the full cell at -20 °C.
- Full cell tested at RT: 103 mAh/g at 0.1 A/g, 353.4 Wh/kg, 80.4% after 3200 cycles at 1 A/g.

So 0391 gives a full cell with an electrolyte containing 5 vol% FEC and cathode low-temperature performance, but the full cell at -20 °C is not clearly reported.

Important: the paper title says "for high energy density sodium ion batteries at −20 °C" — so the -20 °C refers to the cathode half-cell.

Now, we have two "candidate electrolyte formulations" for the NVPF||HC full cell:
1. E1 (0036 Lin 2019): 1 M NaClO4 in EC:PC (1:1 v/v) — measured in the exact target full cell at 25/0/-20 °C. At -20 °C fast capacity fading.
2. E2 (0391 Lei 2024): 1 M NaClO4 in EC:PC (1:1 v/v) + 5 vol% FEC — measured in the target full cell (NVPF||HC, pre-sodiated HC) at RT; cathode half-cell at -20 °C shows excellent retention.
3. E3 (0023 Hu 2024): 0.8 M NaPF6 + 0.2 M NaBF4 in DEGDME (BPG) — NVPF||HC full cell at -10/25/60 °C; cathode at -25 °C.
4. E4 (0070 Xia 2025): 1 M NaDFOB in G2 — HC//NFPP pouch -40 to 60 °C; NVPF electrode tested over 200 cycles (RT).
5. E5 (0033 Li 2026): 0.8 M NaPF6 in G2:MO = 7:3 vol% (CIE) — HC||NFM pouch, -20 °C 94.1% retention after 300 cycles, -50 °C operation. Cathode is NFM not NVPF.

Now the sodium-plating capacity limit at -20 °C: 
- Core quantitative answer from 0036: 250 mAh g⁻¹ (based on HC anode mass), = ~80% of RT HC capacity; plating onset ~300 mAh/g (CE 95.3%); Na metal at 350, dendrites at 450 mAh/g.
- Also 0036 states the full cell at -20 °C: significant drop within first 5 cycles; after 10 cycles at -20 °C, returning to 25 °C recovers ~82%.
- 0036's full cell at 25 °C: 306 mAh g⁻¹ (anode basis), 310 Wh/kg, 3.62 V.

So the "reversible no-plating capacity limit" for the NVPF||HC full cell at -20 °C ≈ 250 mAh g⁻¹ based on the hard-carbon anode mass, which is the anode-limited cap. In the full cell this corresponds to capping the anode utilization at 250 mAh/g. 

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: at -20 °C the full cell's real capacity is well below 250 due to polarization. So the "limit" is a ceiling not a delivered value. Good — I should state it accurately: literature establishes 250 mAh g⁻¹(HC) as the reversible, plating-free capacity ceiling at -20 °C; the full cell at -20 °C with the carbonate baseline electrolyte delivered much less and faded.

Now, the design decision. The user asks: (a) determine the reversible no-plating capacity limit at -20 °C, and (b) select an appropriate electrolyte.

Both are evidence questions. The capacity limit is directly answered by 0036. For the electrolyte selection, we must screen candidates.

Key evidence gap: no candidate has the NVPF||HC full cell measured at exactly -20 °C with an improved electrolyte. Options:
- E1: exact cell, exact temperature, but the paper itself concludes "there is no need to change the mass ratio" but full cell fades at -20 °C; calls for a more stable SEI. So E1 is the baseline, failing at -20 °C (well, it works but fades).
- E2: same cell + FEC additive; cathode shows 96.8 mAh/g at -20 °C, 95.7% retention after 900 cycles; full cell at RT. FEC is the standard SEI former that 0036 calls for. This is a strong candidate for "appropriate electrolyte" — FEC-containing carbonate electrolyte for the NVPF||HC full cell.
- E3: NVPF||HC full cell with ether dual-salt; -10 °C measured (close to -20 but not -20); cathode at -25 °C. This is the most cathode-matched low-temperature electrolyte with the same cathode family (NVPF, though Hu used Na3V2(PO4)2F3 with carbon-coated nanosheet morphology, not Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3).

Hmm, but for the -20 °C condition and no-plating, an ether electrolyte is attractive since ethers have low desolvation barrier and low freezing point. But ethers co-intercalate into HC and can cause plating issues... Actually for HC in ethers at low temperature, solvent co-intercalation boosts capacity.

I think the honest assessment: 
- The capacity limit (250 mAh/g at -20 °C, HC basis) is well supported by 0036.
- The electrolyte selection: no candidate has a documented no-plating verification at -20 °C in the exact Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3||HC full cell with an improved electrolyte. Therefore the DecisionState will likely be "hold" for recommending an improved electrolyte formulation, or "recommend" the FEC-containing carbonate baseline + verification plan.

Let me define constraints:
1. temperature ≤ -20 °C (kind: temperature, operator <=, value -20, unit °C) — user says "at -20 C" → temperature. Wait, careful: "at -20 C" modifies "full cell" → temperature. Yes. This is a claim to be established: that there exists a reported reversible, plating-free capacity limit for the HC anode at -20 °C in this cell.

additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
Now run screen_formulations with the full constraint set.

Constraints:
1. "cell-full" cell_configuration, evidence_terms ["full cell","full-cell","full cells","full-cell"], required_evidence_scope candidate_same_paper.
2. "electrode-nvpf" electrode_material, evidence_terms ["Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3","Na3V2(PO4)2F3","NVPF"].
3. "electrode-hardcarbon" electrode_material, evidence_terms ["hard carbon","hard-carbon","HC"].
4. "temp-minus20" temperature operator "==" value -20 unit "°C".
5. "conc-present" field_presence field concentration_mol_l.
6. "claim-noplating-limit" evidence_claim.
7. "claim-lt-fullcell-test" evidence_claim.

joint_context_requirements: group "nvpf-hc-fullcell--20C": constraint_ids ["temp-minus20","electrode-nvpf","electrode-hardcarbon","cell-full"], context_fields ["temperature_c","electrode","cell_configuration"], target_context {"temperature_c": -20.0, "electrode": "Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 (cathode) / hard carbon (anode)"}.

Hmm — target_context.electrode. The constraint checker identifies electrode and cell_configuration separately. For the electrode field in target_context, the expected value format? The skill example used {"temperature_c": -20.0, "electrode": "hard carbon"}. I'll use "hard carbon" as the electrode since that's the clearly-stated anode, and NVPF is in constraint_ids via electrode-nvpf. Hmm but joint context requires all listed constraints to be jointly satisfied in the same context. context_fields only lists the fields relevant for the join. If I put electrode: "hard carbon", the join checks the electrode field matches "hard carbon". The NVPF electrode constraint is still a constraint but not part of the context_fields join check. That's acceptable.

Actually to be safe and meaningful, target_context = {"temperature_c": -20.0, "electrode": "hard carbon"}. Since the cathode identity is checked separately by constraint electrode-nvpf, not by the context join.

Hmm, but would including "cell_configuration" in context_fields without a target value cause issue? The instruction: "target_context 只填写用户明确给出的目标条件，未知字段保持未知". The user said "full cell" — that's a cell configuration type but the checker uses "pouch"/"coin" shape names. Since unknown shape, I'll not set cell_configuration in target_context but keep it in context_fields? The field would be unknown → possibly the join fails. Safer: context_fields ["temperature_c","electrode"] and target_context {"temperature_c": -20.0, "electrode": "hard carbon"}. The cell-full constraint still appears in constraint_ids (so the obligation includes full-cell), but the join comparison only uses the listed context_fields.

Hmm, "context_fields 只列对联合决策真正相关的字段". Full cell is highly relevant. But given the label vocabulary (pouch/coin), a full cell isn't one of those labels. I'll include temperature_c and electrode only. Actually, hmm, the skill says joint_context_requirements for full cell: "全电池要求另用 cell_configuration 检查条件和明确的正负极对验证". So cell_configuration is its own check condition (constraint 1) and positive/negative pair via the two electrode_material constraints. That's exactly what I have. So the joint group can focus on temperature + electrode.

Now claim_verdicts:

claim-noplating-limit: claim "该候选电解液所配的 Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3||硬碳全电池体系中，硬碳负极在 -20 °C 存在一个被实验测定的可逆且无钠析出的容量上限（约 250 mAh g⁻¹，基于硬碳质量）"
- c1: supported, chunk 0036::sec6::child11, quote "$250\\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ is regarded as the reversible and safe capacity limitation for HC at $-20^{\\circ}\\mathrm{C}$" — must be verbatim substring. The content: "For the cell cycled at $300\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ , the Coulombic efficiency decreases to only $95.3\%$ due to the Na plating/stripping. Hence the capacity of $250\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ is regarded as the reversible and safe capacity limitation for HC at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ ." I'll quote "the capacity of $250\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ is regarded as the reversible and safe capacity limitation for HC at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$" — verbatim.

Careful: the text uses "\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}" — I must reproduce exactly. I'll copy precisely.

- c2, c3, c4: not_found.

claim-lt-fullcell: claim "该候选电解液已被用于 Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3（或同族 NVPF）正极与硬碳负极组成的全电池并在 -20 °C 下实际充放电测试"
- c1: supported, chunk 0036::sec6::child17, quote "when the full cell was charged/discharged at -20°C, a significant drop in capacity is observed, particularly during the first 5 cycles"
- c2,c3,c4: not_found

Hmm — for c2, the -20 °C data is cathode half-cell against Na. For c3, full cell at -10 °C. So not_found is correct.

Should I also add the requirement about "appropriate electrolyte" selection, i.e., that the electrolyte should show low-temperature capability? I'll add a third claim:
claim-lt-suitability: "该候选电解液在低温（≤ -10 °C）下被报告具有可用的电化学性能（可逆容量或容量保持率）"
- c1: supported? 0036 reports the full cell at -20 °C with capacity and 82% recovery — but "fast capacity fading". Hmm. Let me phrase the claim as "在 -20 °C 或更低温度下被报告具有可逆容量/容量保持率结果" — that's basically what claim-lt-fullcell covers. I'll skip the third claim to avoid redundancy. Actually a claim capturing the electrolyte's own low-temperature report would be useful for the "selecting an appropriate electrolyte" part. Let me phrase:

claim-lt-electrolyte: "该候选电解液自身在 -20 °C（或更低温度）被报告了可用电化学性能（容量保持率或可逆容量数据）"
- c1: supported — 0036 reports the full cell at -20 °C cycling (with capacity data). Hmm, but is it "可用电化学性能"? It faded fast. Not "可用". Let's use neutral phrasing: "该候选电解液在 -20 °C 被报告了容量/循环数据". Same as claim-lt-fullcell essentially. Skip.

OK, two claims are enough. Plus maybe one fact claim in the report.

Actually, let me reconsider whether to make claim-lt-fullcell a "supported" for c1 given the capacity dropped. The claim says "被实际充放电测试并报告了容量" — the quote supports that it was charged/discharged at -20 °C and capacity behavior reported. I'll phrase precisely: "该候选电解液所配的 Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3||硬碳全电池在 -20 °C 被实际充放电测试并报告了容量表现（含衰减）". Good, honest.

Now the screening. Note that the gate may produce "hold" or "recommend". Let's run.

For evidence_terms on cell_configuration: ["full cell", "full cells", "full-cell"].

Also, I should be careful: does the screening give hard failures for temperature == -20 on c2/c3/c4? They have no -20 °C full-cell evidence → insufficient.

Let's submit.

messages.content: One supplementary round found a directly relevant no-plating full-battery source (0180). Let me re-screen with the updated candidate set and the same joint-context contract.

additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
Paper 0180: 1 M NaPF6-G2/DME high-solvation-entropy electrolyte; NVP||HC full battery at -40 °C without Na plating; HC anode 284 mAh/g at 0.06 A/g and 97 mAh/g at 2.10 A/g at -40 °C; 80.60% retention over 1400 cycles at -40 °C; power density 1132.31 W/kg.

But the cathode is Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP), not Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 (NVPF). Still, it's a "no Na plating" full battery with an ether electrolyte and -40 °C operation. It's a valuable candidate: it directly addresses the no-plating requirement in a HC full cell at ultra-low temperature with a specific composition (1 M NaPF6-G2/DME).

But the G2/DME ratio isn't specified in what I retrieved. Hmm — for the candidate I need an explicit concentration (1 M is explicit) and solvent. The ratio of G2:DME is not given in these chunks. I could include it with solvent_ratios empty (basis unknown).

Now: should I add this as a 5th candidate? The semantic review asked for the no-plating limit and NVPF||HC at -20 °C. 0180 is a strong addition for the "no plating at low temperature via electrolyte design" argument, even though the cathode is NVP not NVPF and the temperature is -40 °C (not -20 °C).

Given "每个选项应作为独立候选分别比较", I'll add it as c5. Then re-screen with the same joint context and the same constraints, updating claim_verdicts for all 5 candidates.

Wait — but the rule: "一旦 screen_formulations 返回 hold 或 recommend，不得再尝试重新构建候选". The first screen returned recommendations empty and passed=false. It didn't return hold/recommend explicitly (the results just have passed=false, recommendation=""). The semantic review came back asking me to补取原文或更换候选后重新筛选. So a re-screen is expected (search状态 → 最多一轮补充检索+重新筛选). I've done one supplementary round. Now re-screen and then report.

Let me add c5 and re-run with same constraints and joint context.

For c5, evidence:
- 0180::sec0::child0 (abstract: NVP||HC full battery without Na plating; electrolyte)
- 0180::sec2 (formulation: 1 M NaPF6-G2/DME)
- 0180::sec2::child11 (conclusion-ish: NVP||HC full battery at -40 °C without Na plating; 1 M NaPF6-G2/DME)
- 0180::sec1::child5 (intro: HC potential drops below 0 V → plating)
- 0180::sec3 (conclusion: 284 mAh/g at -40 °C, 80.60% over 1400 cycles)

claim verdicts for c5:
- claim-noplating-limit (about Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3||HC at -20 °C with ~250 mAh/g): the 0180 evidence is about NVP||HC at -40 °C without plating, not a -20 °C limit value for NVPF. So verdict... The claim asserts the candidate's system (Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3||HC) has a measured reversible no-plating capacity limit at -20 °C ≈250 mAh/g. 0180 doesn't establish that (different cathode, different temperature). Honest verdict: not_found. Hmm, but one could argue "supported" for a weaker version. The claim as worded specifies Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 and -20 °C. So not_found.

Hmm, that weakens c5. Alternatively I could add a separate claim for c5: "该候选电解液在其所配的碱金属离子全电池中被报告在低温下无钠析出运行" — but then claim_verdicts must be per candidate for all candidates. Adding a third claim is fine and gives c5 a supported verdict.

Let me add constraint "claim-noplating-lt" : claim "该候选电解液在其报告的全电池/负极体系中，低温（≤ -20 °C）下被报告未发生钠析出（无 Na plating）".
- c1: refuted? The 0036 paper says plating starts to intervene around 300 mAh/g at -20 °C — that means plating occurs above 300 mAh/g. But not "in the full cell". Hmm. For c1, does the source say plating happened in the full cell? No explicit. But it says "sodium plating start to intervene around 300 mAh/g" in the HC half cell at -20 °C. That's a statement that plating does occur beyond 300. Is that "refuted" for c1? The claim says "被报告未发生钠析出" — the source doesn't report absence of plating for the whole operating window; it reports a safe window up to 250. Verdict "not_found" for c1 would be honest but the source does establish a plating onset. Hmm.

Let me instead word the claim more carefully: "该候选电解液所配的电池在低温下被报告为无钠析出（no Na plating）运行". 
- c1: not_found (0036 does not claim no-plating in the full cell; it establishes a safe capacity window at -20 °C). Actually wait — 0036 does effectively report that within 250 mAh/g there is no plating at -20 °C (with in situ XRD/Raman). Hmm, that IS a no-plating statement. "A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g-1 can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C". So supported for the constrained window. But then the semantic review's point stands that the full cell fades.

I think simpler: keep two claims, and for c5 (0180) add its own dedicated claim? No, claim_verdicts must cover submitted candidates.

OK let me restructure to three claims:
A. claim-noplating-limit-20 (≈250 mAh/g at -20 °C in the NVPF||HC system): c1 supported, others not_found.
B. claim-lt-fullcell-20 (electrolyte actually cycled in NVPF||HC full cell at -20 °C): c1 supported, others not_found.
C. claim-no-plating-lt: "该候选电解液在其报道的低温（≤ -20 °C）全电池/负极测试中被报告为无钠析出（no Na plating）": 
  - c1: supported? Source: "A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g-1 can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C, as evidenced by in situ XRD and Raman tests." — that's a no-plating statement at -20 °C. I'd call it supported for the HC electrode at ≤250 mAh/g. But the scope... it's the HC anode, in the same paper's system. Verdict supported with quote and basis noting it holds within the 250 mAh/g cap.
  - c2: not_found
  - c3: not_found

evidence.text: Overall, an unprecedented high-power-density rechargeable NVP||HC full battery has been realized at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ without Na plating on HC anode surface, which can be attributed to the following three aspects: a) the designed high-solvation-entropy electrolyte (1 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2/DME) with a small solvation cluster size possesses elevated ionic conductivity and larger $t_{Na}^{+}$ value at low temperatures compared with conventional electrolytes, facilitating $Na^{+}$ migration to the HC surface; b) a thin, NaF-rich SEI layer with small interfacial resistance is generated on the HC anode surface in the designed electrolyte, promoting $Na^{+}$ transport through the SEI; c) fast kinetics lowers the electrochemical polarization, hence suppressing Na plating on the HC anode.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0
evidence_chunks.content: Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5. The cells were galvanostatic charged/discharged with a LAND 2001 CT battery test system (Wuhan, China) under various voltage ranges and current rates. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out on a VMP system (Biologic S.A., Claix, France).

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child16
evidence_chunks.content: The voltage profiles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell consists of a plateau at 4.1 V and sloping regime between 3.6-2.5 V, contributing to an accumulative capacity of 306 mAh g $^{-1}$ (based on the mass of anode). The energy density is calculated to be 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ based on the total weight of cathode and anode, along with an average discharge potential of 3.62 V. A stable cyclic performance similar to that in half-cell is achieved at $25^{\circ}$ C, as indicated by full cell F1 in Figure 5b. Ulteriorly, we tested the behavior of full cell under low temperature. Firstly, the performance of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ half-cell at 0°C and -20°C are measured and given in Figure S7a and S7b. The reversible capacity decreases with lowering the temperature. It maintains 93.2% and 80.4% of the capacity at room temperature for testing at 0°C and -20°C, respectively. Nevertheless, cyclic stability is kept. It is worthwhile to mention that the safe capacity for HC working at -20°C is 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ , which is also around 80% of its capacity at room temperature. Therefore, there is no need to change the mass ratio of the cathode and anode in the full cell for operating at low temperature.

For the cell cycled at $300\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ , the Coulombic efficiency decreases to only $95.3\%$ due to the Na plating/stripping. Hence the capacity of $250\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ is regarded as the reversible and safe capacity limitation for HC at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ .

![](images/88294c35b5287333781f185b5dfed6bfa118e5e1ab7483c2a55686fd66a291f2.jpg)

![](images/40e5827143f5d2e95de3ccac26fcdfd5652784f11eae524e93213e6095faa6c1.jpg)

![](images/b648b66100c69caca5a474837f8abd3a419c221160f5107c39cd2f37680c45a6.jpg)  
Figure 3a) In situ XRD pattern of HC cycled at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . b) Voltage profiles of HC half-cell at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ with a capacity limitation of $250\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ . c) Low-temperature performance of HC electrodes prepared with different binder materials. Moreover, in situ Raman is adopted to investigate the ion storage behavior of HC at low temperature, and optical images were taken concomitantly. Figure S5 indicates no significant changes in Raman patterns during the entire discharge process, and the spectra are similar to that collected at $25^{\circ}$ C, advocating the same sodium storage mechanism in HC at both low and room temperature. The optical images in Figure S6 clearly indicate the formation of Na metal at the capacity of $350\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . Sodium dendrite could be recognized at the capacity of $450\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ .

The solution consisted of 1 M NaClO $_{4}$ dissolved in ethylene carbonate

(EC) and propylene carbonate (PC) (1:1 in $\nu/\mathrm{v}$ ) with 5 vol% fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) was employed as an electrolyte. The electrochemical performance was tested by CR2032 coin-type. The working electrodes were prepared by mixing 70 wt% active material, 20 wt% acetylene black and 10 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF). The slurry was coated on carbon-coated the Al foil and dried at 60 °C for 12 h in vacuum oven to obtain the testing electrodes. Two electrolytes were used for electrochemical tests. The dual-anion regulated electrolyte was prepared consisting of 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ and 0.2 M NaBF $_{4}$ in diethyleneglycol dimethyl ether. The electrolyte of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in propylene carbonate (PC) was selected as the reference electrolyte. The loading mass of the active material in the electrode was about 1.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . The anode was pure Na metal foil and the separator was glass fiber (GF/D). The full cell was assembled by using HM-NVPF@CN cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode in BPG electrolyte. Before assembling the full cell, the hard carbon anode was pre-cycled for several cycles to form a stable electrode-electrolyte interface. Galvanostatic charge/discharge (GCD) and galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) tests were conducted on a Neware system (CT-4008T-5V10mA-164, Shenzhen, China). source_refs.raw_quote: Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5. The cells were galvanostatic charged/discharged with a LAND 2001 CT battery test system (Wuhan, China) under various voltage ranges and current rates. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out on a VMP system (Biologic S.A., Claix, France).

source_refs.raw_quote: The voltage profiles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell consists of a plateau at 4.1 V and sloping regime between 3.6-2.5 V, contributing to an accumulative capacity of 306 mAh g $^{-1}$ (based on the mass of anode). The energy density is calculated to be 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ based on the total weight of cathode and anode, along with an average discharge potential of 3.62 V. A stable cyclic performance similar to that in half-cell is achieved at $25^{\circ}$ C, as indicated by full cell F1 in Figure 5b. Ulteriorly, we tested the behavior of full cell under low temperature. Firstly, the performance of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ half-cell at 0°C and -20°C are measured and given in Figure S7a and S7b. The reversible capacity decreases with lowering the temperature. It maintains 93.2% and 80.4% of the capacity at room temperature for testing at 0°C and -20°C, respectively. Nevertheless, cyclic stability is kept. It is worthwhile to mention that the safe capacity for HC working at -20°C is 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ , which is also around 80% of its capacity at room temperature. Therefore, there is no need to change the mass ratio of the cathode and anode in the full cell for operating at low temperature.

Figure 3a) In situ XRD pattern of HC cycled at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . b) Voltage profiles of HC half-cell at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ with a capacity limitation of $250\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ . c) Low-temperature performance of HC electrodes prepared with different binder materials. Moreover, in situ Raman is adopted to investigate the ion storage behavior of HC at low temperature, and optical images were taken concomitantly. Figure S5 indicates no significant changes in Raman patterns during the entire discharge process, and the spectra are similar to that collected at $25^{\circ}$ C, advocating the same sodium storage mechanism in HC at both low and room temperature. The optical images in Figure S6 clearly indicate the formation of Na metal at the capacity of $350\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . Sodium dendrite could be recognized at the capacity of $450\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ .

source_refs.raw_quote: The optical images in Figure S6 clearly indicate the formation of Na metal at the capacity of $350\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . Sodium dendrite could be recognized at the capacity of $450\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ . The above results suggest that sodium plating start to intervene around $300\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ , and it will be safe to use HC within the capacity of $250\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The performance of the electrode is not only affected by the active materials but also governed by the other components such as electrolyte and binder. It has been demonstrated by Palacín et al. the importance of electrolyte formulation for the stable performance of HC at low temperature. $^{[21]}$ The binder plays a vital role in maintaining the structural integrity, but its effect under low temperature is not clear yet. Therefore, electrodes using several typical binders, including CMC, NaAg and PVDF are compared in Figure 3c for their low temperature performance. Among the three binders, PVDF exhibits the highest reversible capacity and the smallest resistance drop. This difference can be explained by the thermal stability of binder materials, as well-studied in Li-ion batteries. $^{[29,30]}$ To state in a simple way, PVDF has the lowest glass transition temperature ( $T_{g}$ ) about -38 °C compared to CMC (121.7 °C) and NaAg (95.3 °C).

source_refs.raw_quote: Therefore, there is no need to change the mass ratio of the cathode and anode in the full cell for operating at low temperature. As expected, the $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell also demonstrates a capacity reduction at 0 °C in the first several cycles and reaches stable capacity retention of 244 mAh g $^{-1}$ (F2 in Figure 5b). However, when the full cell was charged/discharged at -20°C, a significant drop in capacity is observed, particularly during the first 5 cycles. It may lie in the increased resistance on the anode side as reflected by EIS. The dynamic property of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ at different temperatures is also evaluated using galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT), as indicated in Figure 5c. From the calculation, the diffusion coefficient of Na-ions ( $D_{Na}^{+}$ ) at 25°C is in the range of $10^{-9}$ to $10^{-10}$ cm $^{2}$ s $^{-1}$ . The value is only slightly decreased at 0°C. In sharp contrast, the $D_{Na}^{+}$ value is about one magnitude lower at -25 °C than that at 25°C. The slow $Na^{+}$ diffusion is in agreement with the EIS results that the thicker SEI film would affect the ion diffusion. After testing at $-20^{\circ}C$ for 10 cycles, the same cell (F3) was put back to $25^{\circ}C$ and its capacity gradually recovered and regained ca. 82% of the capacity at $25^{\circ}C$ .

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, a hard carbon material for NIBs is fabricated from low-cost biomass waste using a facile two-step thermal treatment. Compared to direct high-temperature carbonization, the pre-treatment at a medium temperature is beneficial to avoiding the selfactivation effect of impurities. An appropriate surface area and pore size distribution are obtained, enabling a stable capacity of around 300 mAh g $^{-1}$ . It also shows excellent performance at a temperature as low as -20 °C. A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C, as evidenced by in situ XRD and Raman tests. As-prepared HC also delivers stable performance in the full cell coupling with a $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ cathode, demonstrated an energy density of 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ (based on the total weight of electrode) with decent cyclic stability at room temperature. Nevertheless, the full cell shows a fast capacity fading at -20 °C due to both the increased resistance and continuous consumption of Na ions. It calls for building stable SEI under low temperature in future studies.

All button cells (CR2032-type) were assembled in an argon-filled glovebox (MIKROUNA of Universal, $O_{2} < 0.01$ ppm, $H_{2}O < 0.01$ ppm). As for the fabrication of the positive electrode, a uniform slurry (active material, carbon black, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 6:3:1 mixed in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidinone) was coated on the aluminum foil and dried in vacuum at 70 °C for 12 h. The mass of active material loading was controlled at 1–2 mg. Metallic sodium plate was used as anode, and glass fiber (Whatman, GF/F) was used as separator. (EC) and propylene carbonate (PC) (1:1 in $\nu/\mathrm{v}$ ) with 5 vol% fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) was employed as an electrolyte. 2.3. Electrochemical measurements
The electrochemical performance was tested by CR2032 coin-type. The working electrodes were prepared by mixing 70 wt% active material, 20 wt% acetylene black and 10 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF). The slurry was coated on carbon-coated the Al foil and dried at 60 °C for 12 h in vacuum oven to obtain the testing electrodes. Two electrolytes were used for electrochemical tests. The dual-anion regulated electrolyte was prepared consisting of 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ and 0.2 M NaBF $_{4}$ in diethyleneglycol dimethyl ether. The electrolyte of 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ in propylene carbonate (PC) was selected as the reference electrolyte. The loading mass of the active material in the electrode was about 1.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . source_refs.raw_quote: Overall, an unprecedented high-power-density rechargeable NVP||HC full battery has been realized at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ without Na plating on HC anode surface, which can be attributed to the following three aspects: a) the designed high-solvation-entropy electrolyte (1 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2/DME) with a small solvation cluster size possesses elevated ionic conductivity and larger $t_{Na}^{+}$ value at low temperatures compared with conventional electrolytes, facilitating $Na^{+}$ migration to the HC surface; b) a thin, NaF-rich SEI layer with small interfacial resistance is generated on the HC anode surface in the designed electrolyte, promoting $Na^{+}$ transport through the SEI; c) fast kinetics lowers the electrochemical polarization, hence suppressing Na plating on the HC anode.

3. Conclusion
In conclusion, we successfully realize a high-power-density rechargeable sodium-ion full battery operated at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ without Na plating by rational electrolyte modulation. 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -G2/DME electrolyte with small solvation clusters size was designed, enabling high $\sigma$ and t $_{\text{Na}}^{+}$ at low temperatures. Notably, the enhanced CIP structure of the designed electrolyte induces the formation of a thin, anion-derived NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance, facilitating facile Na $^{+}$ transport through the SEI. As a result, the HC anode in the designed electrolyte presents a remarkably high capacity of 284 mAh g $^{-1}$ (0.06 A g $^{-1}$ ) and 97 mAh g $^{-1}$ (2.10 A g $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ , respectively. Impressively, the NVP||HC full battery achieves a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ and exhibits an outstanding capacity retention of 80.60% over 1400 cycles at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ . This work would facilitate the development of low-temperature SIBs for practical power-intensive application scenarios.

source_refs.raw_quote: As the most promising anode material for commercialization in SIBs, hard carbon (HC) possesses a low-potential plateau ( $\approx0.1\ V$ ) with a high capacity, which is favorable for increasing the energy density of full batteries. $^{[21-24]}$ Nevertheless, at low temperatures and high rates, the operating potential of HC can easily drop below 0 V versus $Na^{+}/Na$ due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization, inducing undesirable Na plating on HC anode. $^{[25,26]}$ Therefore, it remains arduous to realize high-power-density HC-based SIBs at low temperatures. Herein, a high-power-density rechargeable HC-based sodium-ion full battery is successfully realized at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ through rational electrolyte chemistry (Scheme 1). Benefited from the high entropy and small solvation clusters of the designed electrolyte, high ionic conductivity and $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ transference number $(\mathrm{t_{Na}^{+}})$ can be achieved at low temperatures. Significantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs in the designed electrolyte induce the formation of a thin, NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance. When paired with $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{V}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (NVP), the full bat tery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C without Na plating. This work sheds light on future development of low-temperature, high-power-density batteries.

source_refs.raw_quote:
ABSTRACT
$Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{2}F_{3}$ (denoted as NVPF) is an attractive cathode for sodium ion batteries (NIB) owning to its high theoretical capacity (128 mAh g $^{-1}$ ) and high working potential (3.9 V vs Na/Na $^{+}$ ). However, NVPF often suffers from low electronic conductivity and unstable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), seriously hindering its practical application. Here, a uniform NVPF microsphere assembled by carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets (HM-NVPF@CN) is prepared and subsequently an inorganic-rich B, F species CEI layer on its surface in dual-anion ether electrolyte is constructed to address above drawbacks. The carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets can shorten the diffusion pathway for both Na $^{+}$ and e $^{-}$ , and provide large electrochemical reaction area. In addition, the robust CEI layer can enhance the Na $^{+}$ transport and suppress the parasitic reactions. The optimized electrode exhibits a good cycling stability (70 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 2000 cycles) and outstanding low temperature performance (99 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -25 °C). The full cell fabricated with a hard carbon (HC) anode achieves a high capacity retention (88% after 930 cycles) and superior high temperature performance (60 °C, 72 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 5C). This work provides a novel idea to regulate interfacial chemistry of cathodes for the high-voltage NIB.

Sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB), which has non-localized electrons in the structure and weak bonds between sodium-ions and anions, has shown fascinating properties, such as high conductivity, compatibility with a variety of solvents, and own film-forming characteristics with no need for film-forming additives. $^{[14,29,30]}$ However, the use of NaDFOB as a single salt for electrolytes and their compatibility with different SIB electrodes have rarely been reported.

source_refs.raw_quote:
Miaomiao Xia, Hui Chen, Zhenxu Zheng, Qingfei Meng, $^{*}$ Along Zhao, Xiaoyang Chen, Xinping Ai, Yongjin Fang, $^{*}$ and Yuliang Cao $^{*}$

Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising alternative for next-generation energy storage solutions, driven by the economic and environmental benefits of abundant sodium resources. A pivotal aspect of SIB advancement is the development of advanced electrolytes, which remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a facile and scalable synthesis method for low-cost sodium-difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) is reported and explored its application as a standalone electrolyte salt for SIBs. The NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, solvent compatibility, and the unique capacity to form a dense, robust solid-electrolyte interphase layer on electrode surfaces. As a result, the $\mathrm{Na_{4}Fe_{3}(PO_{4})_{2}P_{2}O_{7}}$ (NFPP) cathode with NaDFOB-based electrolyte exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability with a remarkable capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles. Furthermore, an Ah-level hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell using NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte shows an impressive cycle life of 500 cycles, coupled with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%. The pouch cells also maintain superior electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range from -40 to 60 °C, showcasing the electrolyte's versatility.

source_refs.raw_quote:
Yingyu Wang, Hao Lan, Shuai Dong, Qiaonan Zhu, Liwei Cheng, Han Wang, Jiawei Wang, Sicong Wang, Mengyao Tang, Kurbanov Mirtemir Shodievich, Gongkai Wang, and Hua Wang\*

High-power-density rechargeable batteries are highly indispensable for power-intensive application scenarios, such as vehicle start-stop system and grid-level frequency regulation. However, realizing high-power-density alkali-ion batteries is challenging especially at low temperatures, as undesirable alkali metal plating tends to occur more easily on the anode surface due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization. Herein, a low-temperature, high-power-density rechargeable $Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ ||hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion full battery without Na plating is realized by electrolyte regulation. The designed high-solvation-entropy electrolyte enables a high ionic conductivity of 13.87 mS cm $^{-1}$ at -40 °C. More importantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs solvation structure induces an anion-derived, thin, NaF-rich solid electrolyte interface (SEI) on HC anodes with low interfacial resistance to ensure facile $Na^{+}$ diffusion through the SEI. Consequently, the assembled sodium-ion full battery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C and 13372.56 W kg $^{-1}$ (132.83 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at 25 °C (based on total mass of the active materials on anode and cathode).

citations.quote: Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5. The cells were galvanostatic charged/discharged with a LAND 2001 CT battery test system (Wuhan, China) under various voltage ranges and current rates. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out on a VMP system (Biologic S.A., Claix, France).

citations.quote: The voltage profiles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell consists of a plateau at 4.1 V and sloping regime between 3.6-2.5 V, contributing to an accumulative capacity of 306 mAh g $^{-1}$ (based on the mass of anode). The energy density is calculated to be 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ based on the total weight of cathode and anode, along with an average discharge potential of 3.62 V. A stable cyclic performance similar to that in half-cell is achieved at $25^{\circ}$ C, as indicated by full cell F1 in Figure 5b. Ulteriorly, we tested the behavior of full cell under low temperature. citations.quote:
Conclusion
In summary, a hard carbon material for NIBs is fabricated from low-cost biomass waste using a facile two-step thermal treatment. Compared to direct high-temperature carbonization, the pre-treatment at a medium temperature is beneficial to avoiding the selfactivation effect of impurities. An appropriate surface area and pore size distribution are obtained, enabling a stable capacity of around 300 mAh g $^{-1}$ . It also shows excellent performance at a temperature as low as -20 °C. A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C, as evidenced by in situ XRD and Raman tests. As-prepared HC also delivers stable performance in the full cell coupling with a $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ cathode, demonstrated an energy density of 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ (based on the total weight of electrode) with decent cyclic stability at room temperature. Nevertheless, the full cell shows a fast capacity fading at -20 °C due to both the increased resistance and continuous consumption of Na ions. It calls for building stable SEI under low temperature in future studies.

citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
$Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{2}F_{3}$ (denoted as NVPF) is an attractive cathode for sodium ion batteries (NIB) owning to its high theoretical capacity (128 mAh g $^{-1}$ ) and high working potential (3.9 V vs Na/Na $^{+}$ ). However, NVPF often suffers from low electronic conductivity and unstable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), seriously hindering its practical application. Here, a uniform NVPF microsphere assembled by carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets (HM-NVPF@CN) is prepared and subsequently an inorganic-rich B, F species CEI layer on its surface in dual-anion ether electrolyte is constructed to address above drawbacks. The carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets can shorten the diffusion pathway for both Na $^{+}$ and e $^{-}$ , and provide large electrochemical reaction area. In addition, the robust CEI layer can enhance the Na $^{+}$ transport and suppress the parasitic reactions. The optimized electrode exhibits a good cycling stability (70 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 2000 cycles) and outstanding low temperature performance (99 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -25 °C). The full cell fabricated with a hard carbon (HC) anode achieves a high capacity retention (88% after 930 cycles) and superior high temperature performance (60 °C, 72 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 5C). This work provides a novel idea to regulate interfacial chemistry of cathodes for the high-voltage NIB.

citations.quote: For example, $NaClO_{4}$ is very explosive and its adsorbed $H_{2}O$ is too difficult to dry out. $^{[28]}$ $NaPF_{6}$ is toxic and expensive, easy to decompose at elevated temperatures and under humidity. $^{[5,14]}$ The NaTFSI and NaFSI are of high cost, and the $TFSI^{-}$ (or $FSI^{-}$ ) anion in NaTFSI (or NaFSI) has a corrosive effect on the aluminum foil collector. $^{[8]}$ Thus, it is of great significance to explore advanced salts to promote the wide applicability of SIBs. Sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB), which has non-localized electrons in the structure and weak bonds between sodium-ions and anions, has shown fascinating properties, such as high conductivity, compatibility with a variety of solvents, and own film-forming characteristics with no need for film-forming additives. $^{[14,29,30]}$ However, the use of NaDFOB as a single salt for electrolytes and their compatibility with different SIB electrodes have rarely been reported.

citations.quote:
Miaomiao Xia, Hui Chen, Zhenxu Zheng, Qingfei Meng, $^{*}$ Along Zhao, Xiaoyang Chen, Xinping Ai, Yongjin Fang, $^{*}$ and Yuliang Cao $^{*}$

Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising alternative for next-generation energy storage solutions, driven by the economic and environmental benefits of abundant sodium resources. A pivotal aspect of SIB advancement is the development of advanced electrolytes, which remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a facile and scalable synthesis method for low-cost sodium-difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) is reported and explored its application as a standalone electrolyte salt for SIBs. The NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, solvent compatibility, and the unique capacity to form a dense, robust solid-electrolyte interphase layer on electrode surfaces. As a result, the $\mathrm{Na_{4}Fe_{3}(PO_{4})_{2}P_{2}O_{7}}$ (NFPP) cathode with NaDFOB-based electrolyte exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability with a remarkable capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles. Furthermore, an Ah-level hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell using NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte shows an impressive cycle life of 500 cycles, coupled with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%. The pouch cells also maintain superior electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range from -40 to 60 °C, showcasing the electrolyte's versatility.

Specifically, the NFPP electrode demonstrates an impressive capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles along with an average CE of 99.96%. citations.chunk_id: 0070_Xia 等 - 2025 - Sodium-DifluorooxalatoBorate-Based Electrolytes for Long-Term Cycle Life and Enhanced Low-Temperat::sec0::child0
citations.quote:
Miaomiao Xia, Hui Chen, Zhenxu Zheng, Qingfei Meng, $^{*}$ Along Zhao, Xiaoyang Chen, Xinping Ai, Yongjin Fang, $^{*}$ and Yuliang Cao $^{*}$

Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising alternative for next-generation energy storage solutions, driven by the economic and environmental benefits of abundant sodium resources. A pivotal aspect of SIB advancement is the development of advanced electrolytes, which remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a facile and scalable synthesis method for low-cost sodium-difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) is reported and explored its application as a standalone electrolyte salt for SIBs. The NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, solvent compatibility, and the unique capacity to form a dense, robust solid-electrolyte interphase layer on electrode surfaces. As a result, the $\mathrm{Na_{4}Fe_{3}(PO_{4})_{2}P_{2}O_{7}}$ (NFPP) cathode with NaDFOB-based electrolyte exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability with a remarkable capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles. Furthermore, an Ah-level hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell using NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte shows an impressive cycle life of 500 cycles, coupled with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%. The pouch cells also maintain superior electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range from -40 to 60 °C, showcasing the electrolyte's versatility.

Specifically, the NFPP electrode demonstrates an impressive capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles along with an average CE of 99.96%. Moreover, the hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell with NaDFOB-diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2) electrolyte shows an extended cycling lifespan of 500 cycles and commendable low-temperature performance. Our findings contribute to the exploration of affordable and functional sodium salts, thereby advancing the practical implementation of SIBs in various applications.

citations.quote:
3. Conclusion
In conclusion, we successfully realize a high-power-density rechargeable sodium-ion full battery operated at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ without Na plating by rational electrolyte modulation. 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -G2/DME electrolyte with small solvation clusters size was designed, enabling high $\sigma$ and t $_{\text{Na}}^{+}$ at low temperatures. Notably, the enhanced CIP structure of the designed electrolyte induces the formation of a thin, anion-derived NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance, facilitating facile Na $^{+}$ transport through the SEI. As a result, the HC anode in the designed electrolyte presents a remarkably high capacity of 284 mAh g $^{-1}$ (0.06 A g $^{-1}$ ) and 97 mAh g $^{-1}$ (2.10 A g $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ , respectively. Impressively, the NVP||HC full battery achieves a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ and exhibits an outstanding capacity retention of 80.60% over 1400 cycles at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ . This work would facilitate the development of low-temperature SIBs for practical power-intensive application scenarios.

citations.chunk_id: 0180_A HighPower Rechargeable SodiumIon Full Battery Operating at 40 C::sec1::child5
citations.quote: As the most promising anode material for commercialization in SIBs, hard carbon (HC) possesses a low-potential plateau ( $\approx0.1\ V$ ) with a high capacity, which is favorable for increasing the energy density of full batteries. $^{[21-24]}$ Nevertheless, at low temperatures and high rates, the operating potential of HC can easily drop below 0 V versus $Na^{+}/Na$ due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization, inducing undesirable Na plating on HC anode. $^{[25,26]}$ Therefore, it remains arduous to realize high-power-density HC-based SIBs at low temperatures. Herein, a high-power-density rechargeable HC-based sodium-ion full battery is successfully realized at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ through rational electrolyte chemistry (Scheme 1). Benefited from the high entropy and small solvation clusters of the designed electrolyte, high ionic conductivity and $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ transference number $(\mathrm{t_{Na}^{+}})$ can be achieved at low temperatures. Significantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs in the designed electrolyte induce the formation of a thin, NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance. When paired with $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{V}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (NVP), the full bat tery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C without Na plating. This work sheds light on future development of low-temperature, high-power-density batteries.

citations.chunk_id: 0180_A HighPower Rechargeable SodiumIon Full Battery Operating at 40 C::sec0::child0
citations.quote:
Yingyu Wang, Hao Lan, Shuai Dong, Qiaonan Zhu, Liwei Cheng, Han Wang, Jiawei Wang, Sicong Wang, Mengyao Tang, Kurbanov Mirtemir Shodievich, Gongkai Wang, and Hua Wang\*

High-power-density rechargeable batteries are highly indispensable for power-intensive application scenarios, such as vehicle start-stop system and grid-level frequency regulation. However, realizing high-power-density alkali-ion batteries is challenging especially at low temperatures, as undesirable alkali metal plating tends to occur more easily on the anode surface due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization. Herein, a low-temperature, high-power-density rechargeable $Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ ||hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion full battery without Na plating is realized by electrolyte regulation. The designed high-solvation-entropy electrolyte enables a high ionic conductivity of 13.87 mS cm $^{-1}$ at -40 °C. More importantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs solvation structure induces an anion-derived, thin, NaF-rich solid electrolyte interface (SEI) on HC anodes with low interfacial resistance to ensure facile $Na^{+}$ diffusion through the SEI. Consequently, the assembled sodium-ion full battery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C and 13372.56 W kg $^{-1}$ (132.83 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at 25 °C (based on total mass of the active materials on anode and cathode).

3. Conclusion
In conclusion, we successfully realize a high-power-density rechargeable sodium-ion full battery operated at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ without Na plating by rational electrolyte modulation. 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -G2/DME electrolyte with small solvation clusters size was designed, enabling high $\sigma$ and t $_{\text{Na}}^{+}$ at low temperatures. Notably, the enhanced CIP structure of the designed electrolyte induces the formation of a thin, anion-derived NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance, facilitating facile Na $^{+}$ transport through the SEI. As a result, the HC anode in the designed electrolyte presents a remarkably high capacity of 284 mAh g $^{-1}$ (0.06 A g $^{-1}$ ) and 97 mAh g $^{-1}$ (2.10 A g $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ , respectively. Impressively, the NVP||HC full battery achieves a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ and exhibits an outstanding capacity retention of 80.60% over 1400 cycles at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ . This work would facilitate the development of low-temperature SIBs for practical power-intensive application scenarios.

association_citations.quote: As the most promising anode material for commercialization in SIBs, hard carbon (HC) possesses a low-potential plateau ( $\approx0.1\ V$ ) with a high capacity, which is favorable for increasing the energy density of full batteries. $^{[21-24]}$ Nevertheless, at low temperatures and high rates, the operating potential of HC can easily drop below 0 V versus $Na^{+}/Na$ due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization, inducing undesirable Na plating on HC anode. $^{[25,26]}$ Therefore, it remains arduous to realize high-power-density HC-based SIBs at low temperatures. Herein, a high-power-density rechargeable HC-based sodium-ion full battery is successfully realized at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ through rational electrolyte chemistry (Scheme 1). Benefited from the high entropy and small solvation clusters of the designed electrolyte, high ionic conductivity and $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ transference number $(\mathrm{t_{Na}^{+}})$ can be achieved at low temperatures. Significantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs in the designed electrolyte induce the formation of a thin, NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance. When paired with $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{V}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (NVP), the full bat tery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C without Na plating. This work sheds light on future development of low-temperature, high-power-density batteries.

In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out on a VMP system (Biologic S.A., Claix, France).

3. Conclusion
In conclusion, we successfully realize a high-power-density rechargeable sodium-ion full battery operated at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ without Na plating by rational electrolyte modulation. 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -G2/DME electrolyte with small solvation clusters size was designed, enabling high $\sigma$ and t $_{\text{Na}}^{+}$ at low temperatures. Notably, the enhanced CIP structure of the designed electrolyte induces the formation of a thin, anion-derived NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance, facilitating facile Na $^{+}$ transport through the SEI. As a result, the HC anode in the designed electrolyte presents a remarkably high capacity of 284 mAh g $^{-1}$ (0.06 A g $^{-1}$ ) and 97 mAh g $^{-1}$ (2.10 A g $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ , respectively. Impressively, the NVP||HC full battery achieves a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ and exhibits an outstanding capacity retention of 80.60% over 1400 cycles at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ . This work would facilitate the development of low-temperature SIBs for practical power-intensive application scenarios.

evidence_ledger.quote: As the most promising anode material for commercialization in SIBs, hard carbon (HC) possesses a low-potential plateau ( $\approx0.1\ V$ ) with a high capacity, which is favorable for increasing the energy density of full batteries. $^{[21-24]}$ Nevertheless, at low temperatures and high rates, the operating potential of HC can easily drop below 0 V versus $Na^{+}/Na$ due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization, inducing undesirable Na plating on HC anode. $^{[25,26]}$ Therefore, it remains arduous to realize high-power-density HC-based SIBs at low temperatures. Herein, a high-power-density rechargeable HC-based sodium-ion full battery is successfully realized at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ through rational electrolyte chemistry (Scheme 1). Benefited from the high entropy and small solvation clusters of the designed electrolyte, high ionic conductivity and $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ transference number $(\mathrm{t_{Na}^{+}})$ can be achieved at low temperatures. Significantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs in the designed electrolyte induce the formation of a thin, NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance. When paired with $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{V}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (NVP), the full bat tery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C without Na plating. This work sheds light on future development of low-temperature, high-power-density batteries.

It can be concluded that the nanosheet-assembled NVPF spheres can effectively alleviate interfacial strain, keep structural stability, and extend cyclic lifespan. Fig. 1c shows the preparation process of modified electrode. A robust inorganic-rich NaF and $\mathrm{NaB_xO_y}$ species CEI layer on HM-NVPF@CN surface was spontaneous formed in the dual-salt ether electrolyte (0.8 M $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ and 0.2 M $\mathrm{NaBF_4}$ in DEGDME, denoted as BPG). evidence_ledger.quote:
ABSTRACT
$Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{2}F_{3}$ (denoted as NVPF) is an attractive cathode for sodium ion batteries (NIB) owning to its high theoretical capacity (128 mAh g $^{-1}$ ) and high working potential (3.9 V vs Na/Na $^{+}$ ). However, NVPF often suffers from low electronic conductivity and unstable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), seriously hindering its practical application. Here, a uniform NVPF microsphere assembled by carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets (HM-NVPF@CN) is prepared and subsequently an inorganic-rich B, F species CEI layer on its surface in dual-anion ether electrolyte is constructed to address above drawbacks. The carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets can shorten the diffusion pathway for both Na $^{+}$ and e $^{-}$ , and provide large electrochemical reaction area. In addition, the robust CEI layer can enhance the Na $^{+}$ transport and suppress the parasitic reactions. The optimized electrode exhibits a good cycling stability (70 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 2000 cycles) and outstanding low temperature performance (99 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -25 °C). The full cell fabricated with a hard carbon (HC) anode achieves a high capacity retention (88% after 930 cycles) and superior high temperature performance (60 °C, 72 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 5C). This work provides a novel idea to regulate interfacial chemistry of cathodes for the high-voltage NIB.

evidence_ledger.quote: For example, $NaClO_{4}$ is very explosive and its adsorbed $H_{2}O$ is too difficult to dry out. $^{[28]}$ $NaPF_{6}$ is toxic and expensive, easy to decompose at elevated temperatures and under humidity. $^{[5,14]}$ The NaTFSI and NaFSI are of high cost, and the $TFSI^{-}$ (or $FSI^{-}$ ) anion in NaTFSI (or NaFSI) has a corrosive effect on the aluminum foil collector. $^{[8]}$ Thus, it is of great significance to explore advanced salts to promote the wide applicability of SIBs. Sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB), which has non-localized electrons in the structure and weak bonds between sodium-ions and anions, has shown fascinating properties, such as high conductivity, compatibility with a variety of solvents, and own film-forming characteristics with no need for film-forming additives. $^{[14,29,30]}$ However, the use of NaDFOB as a single salt for electrolytes and their compatibility with different SIB electrodes have rarely been reported.

evidence_ledger.quote:
Miaomiao Xia, Hui Chen, Zhenxu Zheng, Qingfei Meng, $^{*}$ Along Zhao, Xiaoyang Chen, Xinping Ai, Yongjin Fang, $^{*}$ and Yuliang Cao $^{*}$

Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising alternative for next-generation energy storage solutions, driven by the economic and environmental benefits of abundant sodium resources. A pivotal aspect of SIB advancement is the development of advanced electrolytes, which remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a facile and scalable synthesis method for low-cost sodium-difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) is reported and explored its application as a standalone electrolyte salt for SIBs. The NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, solvent compatibility, and the unique capacity to form a dense, robust solid-electrolyte interphase layer on electrode surfaces. As a result, the $\mathrm{Na_{4}Fe_{3}(PO_{4})_{2}P_{2}O_{7}}$ (NFPP) cathode with NaDFOB-based electrolyte exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability with a remarkable capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles. Furthermore, an Ah-level hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell using NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte shows an impressive cycle life of 500 cycles, coupled with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%. The pouch cells also maintain superior electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range from -40 to 60 °C, showcasing the electrolyte's versatility.

The NaDFOB facilitates the formation of a dense and robust cathode-electrolyte interface (CEI) layer on the $\mathrm{Na_{3}Fe_{2}(PO_{4})P_{2}O_{7}}$ (NFPP) cathode, significantly enhances its cyclability and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Specifically, the NFPP electrode demonstrates an impressive capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles along with an average CE of 99.96%. Moreover, the hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell with NaDFOB-diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2) electrolyte shows an extended cycling lifespan of 500 cycles and commendable low-temperature performance. Our findings contribute to the exploration of affordable and functional sodium salts, thereby advancing the practical implementation of SIBs in various applications.

evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0180_A HighPower Rechargeable SodiumIon Full Battery Operating at 40 C
evidence_ledger.quote:
Yingyu Wang, Hao Lan, Shuai Dong, Qiaonan Zhu, Liwei Cheng, Han Wang, Jiawei Wang, Sicong Wang, Mengyao Tang, Kurbanov Mirtemir Shodievich, Gongkai Wang, and Hua Wang\*

High-power-density rechargeable batteries are highly indispensable for power-intensive application scenarios, such as vehicle start-stop system and grid-level frequency regulation. However, realizing high-power-density alkali-ion batteries is challenging especially at low temperatures, as undesirable alkali metal plating tends to occur more easily on the anode surface due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization. Herein, a low-temperature, high-power-density rechargeable $Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ ||hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion full battery without Na plating is realized by electrolyte regulation. The designed high-solvation-entropy electrolyte enables a high ionic conductivity of 13.87 mS cm $^{-1}$ at -40 °C. More importantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs solvation structure induces an anion-derived, thin, NaF-rich solid electrolyte interface (SEI) on HC anodes with low interfacial resistance to ensure facile $Na^{+}$ diffusion through the SEI. Consequently, the assembled sodium-ion full battery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C and 13372.56 W kg $^{-1}$ (132.83 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at 25 °C (based on total mass of the active materials on anode and cathode).

citations.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0
citations.quote: Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. Two pieces of Whatman glass fibers soaked with the electrolyte were used as the separator between the positive and negative electrode. The HC electrode was prepared by casting a slurry of 90 wt% HC, 5 wt% conductive carbon black and 5 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder on copper foil. In companions, electrodes using carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt (CMC) and sodium alginate (NaAg) as the binder were also prepared. Typical loading mass of the HC electrode was around 1.5 mg cm $^{-2}$ . For the full cell, Na $_{3.5}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{2}$ F $_{3}$ powders were mixed with 20% carbon SP for the preparation of positive electrodes. The weight ratio of the positive/negative electrodes was 2.5. The cells were galvanostatic charged/discharged with a LAND 2001 CT battery test system (Wuhan, China) under various voltage ranges and current rates. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was carried out on a VMP system (Biologic S.A., Claix, France).

citations.quote: The voltage profiles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell consists of a plateau at 4.1 V and sloping regime between 3.6-2.5 V, contributing to an accumulative capacity of 306 mAh g $^{-1}$ (based on the mass of anode). The energy density is calculated to be 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ based on the total weight of cathode and anode, along with an average discharge potential of 3.62 V. A stable cyclic performance similar to that in half-cell is achieved at $25^{\circ}$ C, as indicated by full cell F1 in Figure 5b. Ulteriorly, we tested the behavior of full cell under low temperature. Firstly, the performance of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ half-cell at 0°C and -20°C are measured and given in Figure S7a and S7b. The reversible capacity decreases with lowering the temperature. It maintains 93.2% and 80.4% of the capacity at room temperature for testing at 0°C and -20°C, respectively. Nevertheless, cyclic stability is kept. It is worthwhile to mention that the safe capacity for HC working at -20°C is 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ , which is also around 80% of its capacity at room temperature. Therefore, there is no need to change the mass ratio of the cathode and anode in the full cell for operating at low temperature.

citations.chunk_id: 0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec7
citations.quote:
Conclusion
In summary, a hard carbon material for NIBs is fabricated from low-cost biomass waste using a facile two-step thermal treatment. Compared to direct high-temperature carbonization, the pre-treatment at a medium temperature is beneficial to avoiding the selfactivation effect of impurities. An appropriate surface area and pore size distribution are obtained, enabling a stable capacity of around 300 mAh g $^{-1}$ . It also shows excellent performance at a temperature as low as -20 °C. A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C, as evidenced by in situ XRD and Raman tests. As-prepared HC also delivers stable performance in the full cell coupling with a $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ cathode, demonstrated an energy density of 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ (based on the total weight of electrode) with decent cyclic stability at room temperature. Nevertheless, the full cell shows a fast capacity fading at -20 °C due to both the increased resistance and continuous consumption of Na ions. It calls for building stable SEI under low temperature in future studies.

citations.quote: Therefore, there is no need to change the mass ratio of the cathode and anode in the full cell for operating at low temperature. As expected, the $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell also demonstrates a capacity reduction at 0 °C in the first several cycles and reaches stable capacity retention of 244 mAh g $^{-1}$ (F2 in Figure 5b). However, when the full cell was charged/discharged at -20°C, a significant drop in capacity is observed, particularly during the first 5 cycles. It may lie in the increased resistance on the anode side as reflected by EIS. The dynamic property of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ at different temperatures is also evaluated using galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT), as indicated in Figure 5c. From the calculation, the diffusion coefficient of Na-ions ( $D_{Na}^{+}$ ) at 25°C is in the range of $10^{-9}$ to $10^{-10}$ cm $^{2}$ s $^{-1}$ . The value is only slightly decreased at 0°C. In sharp contrast, the $D_{Na}^{+}$ value is about one magnitude lower at -25 °C than that at 25°C. The slow $Na^{+}$ diffusion is in agreement with the EIS results that the thicker SEI film would affect the ion diffusion. After testing at $-20^{\circ}C$ for 10 cycles, the same cell (F3) was put back to $25^{\circ}C$ and its capacity gradually recovered and regained ca. 82% of the capacity at $25^{\circ}C$ .

3. Results and discussion
To evaluate the impacts of NVPF microstructure on the cyclic stability for achieving remarkable long cycle life, the von mises stress distribution of solid NVPF sphere and nanosheet-assembled NVPF sphere were calculated by COMSOL finite element simulation in Fig. 1a. The unique 2D structure can effectively release strain distribution caused by volume expansion and ensure the structural stability of electrode compared to the granular structure during the repeated sodiation/desodiation process, resulting in the excellent cycling stability. In Fig. 1b, the maximum stress of solid NVPF sphere is 6.53 MPa, which is much larger than that of nanosheet-assembled NVPF sphere (2.68 MPa). The huge stress distribution on the solid NVPF sphere surface, which easy cause structural fracture of solid NVPF sphere during the repeated insertion/extraction of the large size of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ , even worse, resulting in battery fails. It can be concluded that the nanosheet-assembled NVPF spheres can effectively alleviate interfacial strain, keep structural stability, and extend cyclic lifespan. Fig. 1c shows the preparation process of modified electrode. A robust inorganic-rich NaF and $\mathrm{NaB_xO_y}$ species CEI layer on HM-NVPF@CN surface was spontaneous formed in the dual-salt ether electrolyte (0.8 M $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ and 0.2 M $\mathrm{NaBF_4}$ in DEGDME, denoted as BPG). The obtained electrode denoted as HM-NVPF@CN-BPG. This special designed CEI layer can effectively protect the active electrode material from the electrolyte corrosion and enhance the Na-ion transport kinetics, resulting in the outstanding electrochemical performance.
