citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
$Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{2}F_{3}$ (denoted as NVPF) is an attractive cathode for sodium ion batteries (NIB) owning to its high theoretical capacity (128 mAh g $^{-1}$ ) and high working potential (3.9 V vs Na/Na $^{+}$ ). However, NVPF often suffers from low electronic conductivity and unstable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), seriously hindering its practical application. Here, a uniform NVPF microsphere assembled by carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets (HM-NVPF@CN) is prepared and subsequently an inorganic-rich B, F species CEI layer on its surface in dual-anion ether electrolyte is constructed to address above drawbacks. The carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets can shorten the diffusion pathway for both Na $^{+}$ and e $^{-}$ , and provide large electrochemical reaction area. In addition, the robust CEI layer can enhance the Na $^{+}$ transport and suppress the parasitic reactions. The optimized electrode exhibits a good cycling stability (70 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 2000 cycles) and outstanding low temperature performance (99 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -25 °C). The full cell fabricated with a hard carbon (HC) anode achieves a high capacity retention (88% after 930 cycles) and superior high temperature performance (60 °C, 72 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 5C). This work provides a novel idea to regulate interfacial chemistry of cathodes for the high-voltage NIB.

The electrochemical performance was tested by CR2032 coin-type. The working electrodes were prepared by mixing 70 wt% active material, 20 wt% acetylene black and 10 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF). 3. Results and discussion
To evaluate the impacts of NVPF microstructure on the cyclic stability for achieving remarkable long cycle life, the von mises stress distribution of solid NVPF sphere and nanosheet-assembled NVPF sphere were calculated by COMSOL finite element simulation in Fig. 1a. The unique 2D structure can effectively release strain distribution caused by volume expansion and ensure the structural stability of electrode compared to the granular structure during the repeated sodiation/desodiation process, resulting in the excellent cycling stability. In Fig. 1b, the maximum stress of solid NVPF sphere is 6.53 MPa, which is much larger than that of nanosheet-assembled NVPF sphere (2.68 MPa). The huge stress distribution on the solid NVPF sphere surface, which easy cause structural fracture of solid NVPF sphere during the repeated insertion/extraction of the large size of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ , even worse, resulting in battery fails. It can be concluded that the nanosheet-assembled NVPF spheres can effectively alleviate interfacial strain, keep structural stability, and extend cyclic lifespan. Fig. 1c shows the preparation process of modified electrode. A robust inorganic-rich NaF and $\mathrm{NaB_xO_y}$ species CEI layer on HM-NVPF@CN surface was spontaneous formed in the dual-salt ether electrolyte (0.8 M $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ and 0.2 M $\mathrm{NaBF_4}$ in DEGDME, denoted as BPG). The obtained electrode denoted as HM-NVPF@CN-BPG. This special designed CEI layer can effectively protect the active electrode material from the electrolyte corrosion and enhance the Na-ion transport kinetics, resulting in the outstanding electrochemical performance.

citations.quote: For example, $NaClO_{4}$ is very explosive and its adsorbed $H_{2}O$ is too difficult to dry out. $^{[28]}$ $NaPF_{6}$ is toxic and expensive, easy to decompose at elevated temperatures and under humidity. $^{[5,14]}$ The NaTFSI and NaFSI are of high cost, and the $TFSI^{-}$ (or $FSI^{-}$ ) anion in NaTFSI (or NaFSI) has a corrosive effect on the aluminum foil collector. $^{[8]}$ Thus, it is of great significance to explore advanced salts to promote the wide applicability of SIBs. Sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB), which has non-localized electrons in the structure and weak bonds between sodium-ions and anions, has shown fascinating properties, such as high conductivity, compatibility with a variety of solvents, and own film-forming characteristics with no need for film-forming additives. $^{[14,29,30]}$ However, the use of NaDFOB as a single salt for electrolytes and their compatibility with different SIB electrodes have rarely been reported.

citations.chunk_id: 0070_Xia 等 - 2025 - Sodium-DifluorooxalatoBorate-Based Electrolytes for Long-Term Cycle Life and Enhanced Low-Temperat::sec0::child0
citations.quote:
Miaomiao Xia, Hui Chen, Zhenxu Zheng, Qingfei Meng, $^{*}$ Along Zhao, Xiaoyang Chen, Xinping Ai, Yongjin Fang, $^{*}$ and Yuliang Cao $^{*}$

Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising alternative for next-generation energy storage solutions, driven by the economic and environmental benefits of abundant sodium resources. A pivotal aspect of SIB advancement is the development of advanced electrolytes, which remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a facile and scalable synthesis method for low-cost sodium-difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) is reported and explored its application as a standalone electrolyte salt for SIBs. The NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, solvent compatibility, and the unique capacity to form a dense, robust solid-electrolyte interphase layer on electrode surfaces. As a result, the $\mathrm{Na_{4}Fe_{3}(PO_{4})_{2}P_{2}O_{7}}$ (NFPP) cathode with NaDFOB-based electrolyte exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability with a remarkable capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles. Furthermore, an Ah-level hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell using NaDFOB-based ether electrolyte shows an impressive cycle life of 500 cycles, coupled with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%. The pouch cells also maintain superior electrochemical performance across a broad temperature range from -40 to 60 °C, showcasing the electrolyte's versatility.

citations.quote: We have thoroughly examined its application as a single salt for the electrolytes of SIBs. The NaDFOB facilitates the formation of a dense and robust cathode-electrolyte interface (CEI) layer on the $\mathrm{Na_{3}Fe_{2}(PO_{4})P_{2}O_{7}}$ (NFPP) cathode, significantly enhances its cyclability and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Specifically, the NFPP electrode demonstrates an impressive capacity retention of 98.7% after 1000 cycles along with an average CE of 99.96%. Moreover, the hard carbon (HC)//NFPP pouch cell with NaDFOB-diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2) electrolyte shows an extended cycling lifespan of 500 cycles and commendable low-temperature performance. Our findings contribute to the exploration of affordable and functional sodium salts, thereby advancing the practical implementation of SIBs in various applications.

In conclusion, we successfully realize a high-power-density rechargeable sodium-ion full battery operated at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ without Na plating by rational electrolyte modulation. 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -G2/DME electrolyte with small solvation clusters size was designed, enabling high $\sigma$ and t $_{\text{Na}}^{+}$ at low temperatures. As a result, the HC anode in the designed electrolyte presents a remarkably high capacity of 284 mAh g $^{-1}$ (0.06 A g $^{-1}$ ) and 97 mAh g $^{-1}$ (2.10 A g $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ , respectively. This work would facilitate the development of low-temperature SIBs for practical power-intensive application scenarios.

citations.chunk_id: 0180_A HighPower Rechargeable SodiumIon Full Battery Operating at 40 C::sec1::child5
citations.quote: As the most promising anode material for commercialization in SIBs, hard carbon (HC) possesses a low-potential plateau ( $\approx0.1\ V$ ) with a high capacity, which is favorable for increasing the energy density of full batteries. $^{[21-24]}$ Nevertheless, at low temperatures and high rates, the operating potential of HC can easily drop below 0 V versus $Na^{+}/Na$ due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization, inducing undesirable Na plating on HC anode. $^{[25,26]}$ Therefore, it remains arduous to realize high-power-density HC-based SIBs at low temperatures. Herein, a high-power-density rechargeable HC-based sodium-ion full battery is successfully realized at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ through rational electrolyte chemistry (Scheme 1). Benefited from the high entropy and small solvation clusters of the designed electrolyte, high ionic conductivity and $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ transference number $(\mathrm{t_{Na}^{+}})$ can be achieved at low temperatures. Significantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs in the designed electrolyte induce the formation of a thin, NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance. When paired with $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{V}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (NVP), the full bat tery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C without Na plating. This work sheds light on future development of low-temperature, high-power-density batteries.

citations.chunk_id: 0180_A HighPower Rechargeable SodiumIon Full Battery Operating at 40 C::sec0::child0
citations.quote:
Yingyu Wang, Hao Lan, Shuai Dong, Qiaonan Zhu, Liwei Cheng, Han Wang, Jiawei Wang, Sicong Wang, Mengyao Tang, Kurbanov Mirtemir Shodievich, Gongkai Wang, and Hua Wang\*

High-power-density rechargeable batteries are highly indispensable for power-intensive application scenarios, such as vehicle start-stop system and grid-level frequency regulation. However, realizing high-power-density alkali-ion batteries is challenging especially at low temperatures, as undesirable alkali metal plating tends to occur more easily on the anode surface due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization. Herein, a low-temperature, high-power-density rechargeable $Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ ||hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion full battery without Na plating is realized by electrolyte regulation. The designed high-solvation-entropy electrolyte enables a high ionic conductivity of 13.87 mS cm $^{-1}$ at -40 °C. More importantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs solvation structure induces an anion-derived, thin, NaF-rich solid electrolyte interface (SEI) on HC anodes with low interfacial resistance to ensure facile $Na^{+}$ diffusion through the SEI. Consequently, the assembled sodium-ion full battery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C and 13372.56 W kg $^{-1}$ (132.83 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at 25 °C (based on total mass of the active materials on anode and cathode).

Ulteriorly, we tested the behavior of full cell under low temperature. Firstly, the performance of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ half-cell at 0°C and -20°C are measured and given in Figure S7a and S7b. The reversible capacity decreases with lowering the temperature. It maintains 93.2% and 80.4% of the capacity at room temperature for testing at 0°C and -20°C, respectively. Nevertheless, cyclic stability is kept. It is worthwhile to mention that the safe capacity for HC working at -20°C is 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ , which is also around 80% of its capacity at room temperature. citations.quote:
Conclusion
In summary, a hard carbon material for NIBs is fabricated from low-cost biomass waste using a facile two-step thermal treatment. Compared to direct high-temperature carbonization, the pre-treatment at a medium temperature is beneficial to avoiding the selfactivation effect of impurities. An appropriate surface area and pore size distribution are obtained, enabling a stable capacity of around 300 mAh g $^{-1}$ . It also shows excellent performance at a temperature as low as -20 °C. A safe and reversible capacity of 250 mAh g $^{-1}$ can be obtained without Na plating at -20 °C, as evidenced by in situ XRD and Raman tests. As-prepared HC also delivers stable performance in the full cell coupling with a $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ cathode, demonstrated an energy density of 310 Wh kg $^{-1}$ (based on the total weight of electrode) with decent cyclic stability at room temperature. Nevertheless, the full cell shows a fast capacity fading at -20 °C due to both the increased resistance and continuous consumption of Na ions. It calls for building stable SEI under low temperature in future studies.

As expected, the $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell also demonstrates a capacity reduction at 0 °C in the first several cycles and reaches stable capacity retention of 244 mAh g $^{-1}$ (F2 in Figure 5b). However, when the full cell was charged/discharged at -20°C, a significant drop in capacity is observed, particularly during the first 5 cycles. It may lie in the increased resistance on the anode side as reflected by EIS. The dynamic property of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ at different temperatures is also evaluated using galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT), as indicated in Figure 5c. From the calculation, the diffusion coefficient of Na-ions ( $D_{Na}^{+}$ ) at 25°C is in the range of $10^{-9}$ to $10^{-10}$ cm $^{2}$ s $^{-1}$ . The value is only slightly decreased at 0°C. In sharp contrast, the $D_{Na}^{+}$ value is about one magnitude lower at -25 °C than that at 25°C. The slow $Na^{+}$ diffusion is in agreement with the EIS results that the thicker SEI film would affect the ion diffusion. After testing at $-20^{\circ}C$ for 10 cycles, the same cell (F3) was put back to $25^{\circ}C$ and its capacity gradually recovered and regained ca. 82% of the capacity at $25^{\circ}C$ .

All button cells (CR2032-type) were assembled in an argon-filled glovebox (MIKROUNA of Universal, $O_{2} < 0.01$ ppm, $H_{2}O < 0.01$ ppm). citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
$Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{2}F_{3}$ (denoted as NVPF) is an attractive cathode for sodium ion batteries (NIB) owning to its high theoretical capacity (128 mAh g $^{-1}$ ) and high working potential (3.9 V vs Na/Na $^{+}$ ). However, NVPF often suffers from low electronic conductivity and unstable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), seriously hindering its practical application. Here, a uniform NVPF microsphere assembled by carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets (HM-NVPF@CN) is prepared and subsequently an inorganic-rich B, F species CEI layer on its surface in dual-anion ether electrolyte is constructed to address above drawbacks. The carbon-coated NVPF nanosheets can shorten the diffusion pathway for both Na $^{+}$ and e $^{-}$ , and provide large electrochemical reaction area. In addition, the robust CEI layer can enhance the Na $^{+}$ transport and suppress the parasitic reactions. The optimized electrode exhibits a good cycling stability (70 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 2000 cycles) and outstanding low temperature performance (99 mAh g $^{-1}$ at -25 °C). The full cell fabricated with a hard carbon (HC) anode achieves a high capacity retention (88% after 930 cycles) and superior high temperature performance (60 °C, 72 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 5C). This work provides a novel idea to regulate interfacial chemistry of cathodes for the high-voltage NIB.

citations.quote: Overall, an unprecedented high-power-density rechargeable NVP||HC full battery has been realized at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ without Na plating on HC anode surface, which can be attributed to the following three aspects: a) the designed high-solvation-entropy electrolyte (1 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2/DME) with a small solvation cluster size possesses elevated ionic conductivity and larger $t_{Na}^{+}$ value at low temperatures compared with conventional electrolytes, facilitating $Na^{+}$ migration to the HC surface; b) a thin, NaF-rich SEI layer with small interfacial resistance is generated on the HC anode surface in the designed electrolyte, promoting $Na^{+}$ transport through the SEI; c) fast kinetics lowers the electrochemical polarization, hence suppressing Na plating on the HC anode.

citations.chunk_id: 0180_A HighPower Rechargeable SodiumIon Full Battery Operating at 40 C::sec3
citations.quote:
3. Conclusion
In conclusion, we successfully realize a high-power-density rechargeable sodium-ion full battery operated at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ without Na plating by rational electrolyte modulation. 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -G2/DME electrolyte with small solvation clusters size was designed, enabling high $\sigma$ and t $_{\text{Na}}^{+}$ at low temperatures. Notably, the enhanced CIP structure of the designed electrolyte induces the formation of a thin, anion-derived NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance, facilitating facile Na $^{+}$ transport through the SEI. As a result, the HC anode in the designed electrolyte presents a remarkably high capacity of 284 mAh g $^{-1}$ (0.06 A g $^{-1}$ ) and 97 mAh g $^{-1}$ (2.10 A g $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ , respectively. Impressively, the NVP||HC full battery achieves a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ and exhibits an outstanding capacity retention of 80.60% over 1400 cycles at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ . This work would facilitate the development of low-temperature SIBs for practical power-intensive application scenarios.

citations.quote: As the most promising anode material for commercialization in SIBs, hard carbon (HC) possesses a low-potential plateau ( $\approx0.1\ V$ ) with a high capacity, which is favorable for increasing the energy density of full batteries. $^{[21-24]}$ Nevertheless, at low temperatures and high rates, the operating potential of HC can easily drop below 0 V versus $Na^{+}/Na$ due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization, inducing undesirable Na plating on HC anode. $^{[25,26]}$ Therefore, it remains arduous to realize high-power-density HC-based SIBs at low temperatures. Herein, a high-power-density rechargeable HC-based sodium-ion full battery is successfully realized at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ through rational electrolyte chemistry (Scheme 1). Benefited from the high entropy and small solvation clusters of the designed electrolyte, high ionic conductivity and $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ transference number $(\mathrm{t_{Na}^{+}})$ can be achieved at low temperatures. Significantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs in the designed electrolyte induce the formation of a thin, NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance. When paired with $\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{V}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (NVP), the full bat tery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C without Na plating. citations.chunk_id: 0180_A HighPower Rechargeable SodiumIon Full Battery Operating at 40 C::sec0::child0
citations.quote:
Yingyu Wang, Hao Lan, Shuai Dong, Qiaonan Zhu, Liwei Cheng, Han Wang, Jiawei Wang, Sicong Wang, Mengyao Tang, Kurbanov Mirtemir Shodievich, Gongkai Wang, and Hua Wang\*

High-power-density rechargeable batteries are highly indispensable for power-intensive application scenarios, such as vehicle start-stop system and grid-level frequency regulation. However, realizing high-power-density alkali-ion batteries is challenging especially at low temperatures, as undesirable alkali metal plating tends to occur more easily on the anode surface due to the increased electrochemical impedance and polarization. Herein, a low-temperature, high-power-density rechargeable $Na_{3}V_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}$ ||hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion full battery without Na plating is realized by electrolyte regulation. The designed high-solvation-entropy electrolyte enables a high ionic conductivity of 13.87 mS cm $^{-1}$ at -40 °C. More importantly, the enhanced contact-ion pairs solvation structure induces an anion-derived, thin, NaF-rich solid electrolyte interface (SEI) on HC anodes with low interfacial resistance to ensure facile $Na^{+}$ diffusion through the SEI. Consequently, the assembled sodium-ion full battery demonstrates a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at -40 °C and 13372.56 W kg $^{-1}$ (132.83 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at 25 °C (based on total mass of the active materials on anode and cathode).

citations.quote:
3. Conclusion
In conclusion, we successfully realize a high-power-density rechargeable sodium-ion full battery operated at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ without Na plating by rational electrolyte modulation. 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ -G2/DME electrolyte with small solvation clusters size was designed, enabling high $\sigma$ and t $_{\text{Na}}^{+}$ at low temperatures. Notably, the enhanced CIP structure of the designed electrolyte induces the formation of a thin, anion-derived NaF-rich SEI layer on HC anode with small interfacial resistance, facilitating facile Na $^{+}$ transport through the SEI. As a result, the HC anode in the designed electrolyte presents a remarkably high capacity of 284 mAh g $^{-1}$ (0.06 A g $^{-1}$ ) and 97 mAh g $^{-1}$ (2.10 A g $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ , respectively. Impressively, the NVP||HC full battery achieves a record-high power density of 1132.31 W kg $^{-1}$ (with an energy density of 61.94 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ and exhibits an outstanding capacity retention of 80.60% over 1400 cycles at $-40\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ . This work would facilitate the development of low-temperature SIBs for practical power-intensive application scenarios.

评估建议：候选 1M NaClO4/EC:PC(1:1 vol) 确为该体系文献所用，并给出 HC 在 -20 °C 无析钠的 250 mAh g^-1 安全容量；但同一电解液的全电池在 -20 °C 因不稳定 SEI 容量快速衰减，原文明确呼吁优化电解液以构建稳定低温 SEI，因此不足以据此推荐其作为低温全电池的适宜电解液，暂不推荐。
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Electrolyte salt is NaClO4 at 1 M concentration：原文方法部分明确写“1M NaClO4 solution ... was applied as the electrolyte”，与候选盐和浓度一致。 [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0]
- Solvent system is EC/PC at 1:1 by volume：同一方法句给出“ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume)”，与候选溶剂及体积比基准一致。 [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0]
- Electrolyte is employed in the Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3 || hard-carbon full cell：原文说明该电解液用于半电池和全电池，且全电池正极为 Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3、负极为 HC，与目标体系匹配。 [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0][0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child16]
- Determine the reversible no-plating capacity limit of the HC anode at -20 C：原文以原位 XRD/Raman 及光学观察定出 -20 °C 下 250 mAh g^-1 为无析钠的可逆安全容量，300 mAh g^-1 时库仑效率降至 95.3% 出现析钠。 [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child11][0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec7]
- No-plating limit is established for the full cell itself at -20 C：250 mAh g^-1 无析钠结论是在 HC 半电池上测得；原文报告的 -20 °C 全电池呈现明显容量下降（前几循环大幅衰减，10 循环后回 25 °C 仅恢复约 82%），并未给出全电池层面的无析钠上限。 [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child17]
- Electrolyte supports a stable low-temperature full cell (stable SEI)：原文指出 -20 °C 下形成更厚（约 23 nm）且不稳定的 SEI 导致全电池容量快速衰减，并明确结论为未来需优化电解液体系以构建稳定 SEI，说明该碳酸酯电解液并非低温全电池的适宜选择。 [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child15][0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec7::child0]
文献与候选的关联：1M NaClO4/EC:PC(1:1 vol) 是本研究中 HC 半电池与 Na3.5V2(PO4)2F3||HC 全电池实际使用的电解液；250 mAh g^-1 无析钠上限由 HC 半电池的原位 XRD/Raman 与光学观察确立，而全电池在 -20 °C 出现容量快速衰减与更厚/不稳定 SEI，两个测量分属半电池与全电池、不能相互替代。 [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0][0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child11][0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child17]

## 文献依据与已记录的计算结果
- Coin cells (CR2032) were used to test the electrochemical performances. 1M NaClO $_{4}$ solution in a mixture of ethylene carbonate/propylene carbonate (EC/PC) (1:1 in volume) was applied as the electrolyte for the half cell and full cells. [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec5::child0]
- The voltage profiles of $\mathrm{Na}_{3.5}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{2}\mathrm{F}_{3}/\mathrm{HC}$ full cell consists of a plateau at 4.1 V and sloping regime between 3.6-2.5 V, contributing to an accumulative capacity of 306 mAh g $^{-1}$ (based on the mass of anode). [0036_Lin 等 - 2019 - Exploring room- and low-temperature performance of hard carbon material in half and full Na-ion batt::sec6::child16]
- For the cell cycled at $300\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ , the Coulombic efficiency decreases to only $95.3\%$ due to the Na plating/stripping. Hence the capacity of $250\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ is regarded as the reversible and safe capacity limitation for HC at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ .
